title: We Join to Pray, with Wishes Kind
description: We Join to Pray, with Wishes Kind in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 380, “Marriage Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We join to pray, with wish-es kind, A bless-ing, Lord, from Thee, On those who now the bands have twined, Which ne'er may bro-ken be.

lines: We join to pray, with wishes kind,
On those who now the bands have twined,
We know that scenes not always bright
But let there shine o'er all the light
Of love, and truth, and heaven.
Still hand in hand, their journey through,
Mingling their joys as helpers true,
In faith, and trust, and heart, the same,
May each in each still feed the flame

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
